takeaway: High anion gap metabolic acidosis means extra unmeasured anions, as in ketoacidosis and lactic acidosis. Anion gap = (Na+ + K+) - (HCO3- + Cl-). A normal gap acidosis also exists.

question.text: Which of the following conditions is associated with a metabolic acidosis and a high anion gap?

lines.text: A high anion gap means there are extra unmeasured anions in the blood.
The anion gap is sodium plus potassium, minus bicarbonate plus chloride.
When unmeasured anions pile up, like ketones or lactate, the gap rises.
That is exactly what happens in ketoacidosis, the fruity breath of acetone.
Lactic acidosis behaves the same way, with a high gap.
But remember, a metabolic acidosis can also have a normal anion gap.
So the high gap condition here is ketoacidosis.
